name: Anagain

lead: Anagain is a branded extract from pea sprouts used in over-the-counter hair serums and lotions. People use it for thicker, fuller-looking scalp hair, often discussed alongside Redensyl, Capixyl and Baicapil.

The idea is that it shifts signals that favor follicle activity. A short communication in Phytotherapy Research reported that a fluid with 2% pea sprout extract changed expression of hair-growth genes in 10 volunteers. A 2025 review lists it among cosmeceutical hair-loss actives.

paras: Applied as a leave-on scalp serum or lotion on a regular schedule, often alongside other hair-growth actives, with results judged over months.
No safety problems were identified in the sources reviewed, though no large safety data exist. It is a cosmetic ingredient, not an approved hair-loss drug.

angle.text: Anagain is a pea-sprout extract in hair serums, meant to favor follicle activity for thicker-looking hair. Support is a small 10-person gene-expression study.

lead: Anagain (also written AnaGain) is a cosmetic hair-care ingredient derived from the sprouts of the pea plant, marketed in topical hair-growth serums and lotions. It is a branded cosmetic active rather than a drug, and it is discussed in appearance communities alongside other 'hair-growth actives' such as Redensyl, Capixyl and Baicapil.[1]

Published human evidence is limited to small, short studies. A short communication in Phytotherapy Research reported that a fluid containing 2% pea sprout extract applied to a defined scalp zone in 10 volunteers changed the expression of genes relevant to hair growth.[2] A 2025 review of cosmeceutical hair-loss actives lists AnaGain among the ingredients it examines, noting that such products are heavily promoted on social media.[1]
infobox: Cosmetic ingredient; not an approved hair-loss drug

paras: The study identified for pea sprout extract is a small short communication in which 10 volunteers applied a 2% pea sprout extract fluid to a defined scalp area, and researchers measured changes in the expression of hair-growth-related genes.[2] The authors state in their introduction that pea sprout extract has previously been reported to improve hair density when applied topically, and that its effect when taken orally was unknown.[2] No large randomized controlled trial of Anagain against placebo or minoxidil was found in the sources reviewed. Other cosmetic serum studies in the literature involve multi-ingredient products rather than pea sprout extract alone.[3][4]

The ingredient appears in forum discussion mainly as one of several 'alternatives' to finasteride and minoxidil. A 2025 trichology review describes the cosmeceutical hair-serum market as flooded with such actives and says it is driven by social-media marketing, while summarising the clinical evidence available for each ingredient.[1]
